title: Customer X — VPC/On‑Prem Weekly Sync (prep & followups)
content:
Purpose / use: personal prep notes for my weekly sync with Customer X engineering/ops on private deployment (VPC + on‑prem). Keep short bullets to steer meeting and capture owners. This is a scratchpad — will clean up before sharing the light-weight meeting minutes.

Meeting info:
- Regular cadence: Thursdays 10:30 PT (30m)
- Attendees: Customer X infra (Alex G., Noor H.), Customer X security (Daniel K.), Jamal (solutions), Priya (infra lead), Marcus (SRE), Elena (onboarding engineer)
- Goal this week: unblock network & storage acceptance tests; confirm cert/KMS plan for production pilot; align on rollout milestone dates for staging -> prod.

Quick status summary (one‑liner for each area):
- Network: VPC peering in progress; routing rule mismatch discovered between AZs — customer working w/ cloud provider. Blocker: missing proper route for pod egress to monitoring endpoint. (owner: Alex + Customer cloud rep)
- Storage: NFS provisioned on site but performance inconsistent; suspect mount options / MTU mismatch. (owner: Noor / Marcus)
- Certs & KMS: customer prefers KMS-in-cloud for now; we need HSM/KMS integration doc and key rotation plan. (owner: Daniel + Jamal)
- Deployment infra: our Helm chart applied to customer cluster; one node failing readiness due to missing kernel module for A100 drivers (edge case on their older host). (owner: Priya)
- Observability/tracing: metrics pipeline ok but span sampling high; need sampling policy for pilot. (owner: Elena)

Prep: questions to ask in sync
- Network: can you paste the current route table for cross-AZ peering? Specific routes for monitor.redwood.ai:443 present? If not, who will add?
- Storage: Is the NFS server using the customer-provided switch with jumbo frames? What MTU do their hosts report?
- Certs/KMS: do you have a security contact who can sign off on KMS-in-cloud for pilot? Are there compliance constraints preventing cloud KMS?
- Drivers: cluster node image/version for the failing host — can they roll a test kernel/driver patch temporarily?
- Cutover dates: confirm staging acceptance window (we proposed Mar 24–26), any blackouts?

Top blockers to highlight (to escalate if needed):
1) Egress routing to monitoring (blocks canary health checks) — impact: prevents signing off on staging test; escalate to customer cloud account team if not resolved in 48h.
2) NFS instability (throughput variance 40–70% of expected) — affects model downloads and large checkpoint load; needs storage team deep dive.
3) Missing kernel module on 1 host — if we can't get that host healthy, capacity will be reduced and throughput SLO may not be met for pilot.

Proposed agenda (10:30–11:00):
- 10:30–10:33 quick status round (one line each) — Jamal
- 10:33–10:40 deep dive: network & storage blockers (Alex + Noor)
- 10:40–10:46 certs/KMS decision and owner for compliance sign-off (Daniel + Jamal)
- 10:46–10:52 infra blockers (driver/node readiness) and remediation plan (Priya + Marcus)
- 10:52–10:57 rollout milestone confirmations (dates, acceptance criteria) — Jamal
- 10:57–11:00 action items recap and next check-in cadence

My personal notes / phrasing to use in meeting (short):
- "We need concrete owners and ETA for the routing change — without routed egress to our monitoring endpoint the canaries can't complete."
- "If the NFS throughput issue persists, we should plan a fallback: replicate model artifacts to an S3-compatible object store in their VPC as a temporary mitigation."
- "For KMS: we can support cloud KMS for pilot but must capture the rotation and access policy — do you have a SOC contact to sign the short attestation?"

Action items (live capture format: action — owner — due)
- Add route for monitor.redwood.ai:443 to cross-AZ routing table — Alex (customer) — 2026-03-13
- Run NFS perf test with tuned mount options (rsize/wsize, noac) and report IOPS/latency — Noor + Marcus — 2026-03-14
- Provide HSM/KMS integration doc and recommend minimal KMS policy for pilot — Jamal — 2026-03-15
- Test node kernel module workaround (temp driver) on failing host and report readiness — Priya — 2026-03-13
- Prepare staging acceptance checklist (small doc) and share with Customer X before Mar 22 — Elena — 2026-03-18

Risks & mitigation notes:
- Risk: routing fix delayed -> mitigation: run canaries on an alternate egress in their lab (requires local NAT rule) or flip to agent-based health reporting (lower fidelity).
- Risk: NFS flakiness -> mitigation: replicate critical artifacts to object storage and throttle prefetching; prioritize model shards needed for pilot.
- Risk: compliance disallowing cloud KMS -> mitigation: provision customer-managed KMS in their VPC (extra infra work, longer lead).

Followups after meeting (what I'll do):
- Send short minutes + action list to attendees and CC account exec + customer cloud rep.
- Open escalation ticket to cloud account team for routing if not done by EOD Monday.
- Draft the KMS attestation checklist and loop in security for sign-off.

Notes to self (private, may delete later):
- If routing consistently slips, ask Sales to request higher priority with cloud partner (we need staging to happen or Q2 pilot slips).
- Keep an eye on kernel-module fix — if vendor image is too old, we may need to recommend a node replacement plan (budget impact).
- Remember to check SUP-1783 for any recent logs from customer that map to NFS errors.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to slim meeting minutes after sync and put final copy under Confluence.
